title: Heavy rain and gusty winds forecast for Bangkok and several regions

Heavy rain and gusty winds forecast for Bangkok and several regions 
 News
 Heavy rain and gusty winds forecast for Bangkok and several regions
 SUNDAY, NOVEMBER 01, 2026 | Nuttapakron Ngamsopa สลับเป็นเสียงผู้ชาย Play Loading... The Thai Meteorological Department warns of flash floods and landslides as rainfall increases, with waves exceeding 2 metres in thundershowers.
 Unsettled weather, including thundershowers, gusty winds, and isolated heavy rain, is forecast for Bangkok and the Central, East, and South regions, particularly from November 2-6.
 The adverse weather is caused by a high-pressure system from China and an easterly wave that will move across Thailand between November 3-5.
 In Bangkok and the Central region, thundershower coverage will increase to 40-60% from November 4-6, bringing gusty winds and heavy rain.
 Authorities have issued warnings for potential flash floods and mudslides, while mariners are cautioned about waves exceeding 2 meters in areas with thundershowers.
 The Thai Meteorological Department forecasts thundershowers in Thailand on Sunday (November 1, 2026), particularly in the Central region, including Bangkok and surrounding areas, the East and the South, in its outlook through November 6.
 A high-pressure system, or cool air mass, from China over upper Thailand and the South China Sea has weakened but continues to bring easterly winds across Thailand and the Gulf of Thailand.
 Unsettled weather is forecast for November 2–6, with thundershowers, gusty winds and isolated heavy rain as a high-pressure system from China extends over the North, Northeast and South China Sea.
 An easterly wave will also move across the lower Northeast, the East, the Central region, including Bangkok and surrounding areas, the Gulf of Thailand and the South during November 3–5.
 Flood and marine warnings 
 People should beware of thundershowers and gusty winds during this period and avoid open areas or places beneath large trees or unstable billboards.
 Heavy rain and continued rainfall accumulation could cause flash floods, rapid run-off from forested areas and mudslides, particularly on foothill slopes close to waterways and in low-lying areas.
 Waves in the Gulf of Thailand and Andaman Sea will exceed 2 metres in areas with thundershowers throughout the forecast period.
 Mariners should check their routes and proceed with caution, while all vessels, including small boats, should avoid areas with thundershowers.

 North
 Thundershowers will cover 10–30% of the North on November 1 and 3–4, with easterly winds at 10–20 km/h. Coverage will be 30–40% on November 2 and 5–6, with gusty winds, isolated heavy rain and southeasterly winds at the same speeds.
 Minimum temperatures: 20–26°C. Maximum temperatures: 28–35°C.
 Northeast
 Thundershowers will cover 10–30% of the Northeast on November 1–2, mostly in its lower part, with northeasterly winds at 10–20 km/h. Coverage will be 40–60% on November 3–6, with gusty winds, isolated heavy rain and easterly winds at 10–25 km/h.
 Minimum temperatures: 21–25°C. Maximum temperatures: 31–35°C.
 Central region, including Bangkok and vicinity
 Thundershowers will cover 20–40% of each area on November 1–3, with easterly winds at 10–20 km/h. Coverage will be 40–60% in both areas on November 4–6, with gusty winds, isolated heavy rain and southeasterly winds at the same speeds.
 The Central region will have minimum temperatures of 22–27°C and maximums of 32–36°C.
 Bangkok and surrounding areas will have minimum temperatures of 24–28°C and maximums of 32–35°C.
 East
 Thundershowers will cover 30–40% of the region on November 1–2, with easterly winds at 10–30 km/h. Coverage will be 40–60% on November 3–6, with gusty winds, isolated heavy rain and southeasterly winds at the same speeds. Waves will be below 1 metre outside areas with thundershowers during both periods.
 Minimum temperatures: 22–27°C. Maximum temperatures: 31–35°C.
 South
 On each coast, thundershowers will cover 40–60% of the area on November 1–3 and 60–70% on November 4–6. Isolated heavy rain is forecast on the east coast in both periods and on the west coast on November 4–6.
 Wind speeds on both coasts will be 15–30 km/h during November 1–6, with waves of about 1 metre outside areas with thundershowers.
 On the east coast, winds will be easterly from Surat Thani northwards and southeasterly from Nakhon Si Thammarat southwards.
 On the west coast, easterly winds are forecast for November 1–3, becoming southeasterly on November 4–6.
 Minimum temperatures on both coasts will be 23–27°C. Maximums will be 30–36°C on the east coast and 31–36°C on the west coast.
